name: Fidelity Denim
why: Jeans cut, sewn and washed in Los Angeles from Italian Candiani denim, in classic fits.
origin: Founded in 2005 by Jason Trotzuk, who started customizing jeans as a teenager in Vancouver.

notes.denim: cut, sewn, and washed in LA on custom cloth from Italy's Candiani mill — rare among LA denim brands, most of which never name their fabric source
notes.comfort: ultra-soft washed stretch as the founding signature
notes.ital: the Candiani connection — Italian cloth in a Vancouver-to-LA story

notes.craft: Fidelity says it cuts, sews and washes its jeans in Los Angeles and every sampled jean page says Made in the USA, but it names no factory and does not claim to own one. Only one of seven product pages names a mill (Candiani on the Torino Ghost Grey); the rest say 'Italian denim'. A country (and city) of make with a single named mill reads as a 2, borderline 3.

cities: No store of its own in the US · independent menswear shops, and its own site

craft_evidence.owned_d: Site claims production location, not ownership: /pages/made-in-fidelity says 'One of the few remaining brands to cut, sew, wash all of our products in Los Angeles'; homepage 'Cut, sewn, and washed in Los Angeles'. No factory named, no address, no photographs of a plant, no statement that the brand owns it. /pages/about-us says 'in North America' instead of Los Angeles (inconsistent).
craft_evidence.countries: USA 7/7 (sample of 7 men's PDPs: Jimmy Oxford, Jimmy Cambridge, Torino Ghost Grey, Torino Patchouli, 808 Phoenix Blue, Firebird Phoenix Blue, plus selvedge collection check). Men's range is almost entirely jeans; no shirts/outerwear found to sample.
